thread:
Ken L.: Heads-up — saw a perf regression after flipping nvfuser FP8 kernels on a small H100 test cluster. Baseline (fp16 inductor) was ~320 tokens/s, FP8+nvfuser dropped to ~250 tokens/s for long-context traces.
Alex M.: hmm, did you see different kernel paths? nvprof traces or kernel names?
Ken L.: Yes, attaching a short snippet from the trace: `conv1x1_cutlass_fp8_k128` then fallback to `matmul_slowpath_int8` for the last blocks. Looks like quantized GEMM path selection is oscillating mid-sequence.
Maria R.: That sounds like a selection hysteresis problem. Any chance the optimizer is flipping between TE (transformer-engine) tensor-core kernels and nvfuser kernels based on instantaneous occupancy?
Ken L.: Exactly. The runtime logs show: `kernel_choice: nvfuser_fp8->fallback->te_fp8->nvfuser_fp8` within the same request (see below).
Ken L.: ```
// simplified log
req=0x7f
seq=1..1024
kernel_choice[0]=nvfuser_fp8_k128
kernel_choice[5]=fallback_int8_slow
kernel_choice[9]=te_tensorcore_fp8
kernel_choice[12]=nvfuser_fp8_k64
```
Olivia P.: Could be microbatching + KV cache warmup changing seq-len distribution mid-run. When KV replays, many heat-map spikes cause occupancy to dip and then kernel selector picks safer slowpath. Did you capture `seq_len_hist`?
Ken L.: I did. Sequence histogram shows a small head at 1-8 tokens then a long tail at 512-1024. The selector seems to prefer smaller-block nvfuser kernels for short prefixes, then switches to a large-block TE kernel for the tail, then back.
Alex M.: Can you repro with deterministic batching? Try `--batcher=static --microbatch=1 --disable-adaptive-selector` and see if it stabilizes. Also try pinning `TE_FORCE_FALLBACK=1` to force transformer-engine kernels only as a comparison.
Ken L.: Ran that. Static batching + disable selector brings us to 315 tokens/s (good). Forcing TE-only is 330 tokens/s. nvfuser-only (forced) is 340 tokens/s on short contexts but regresses on long tails — so selection logic is failing to pick the optimal kernel for mixed distributions.
Maria R.: Interesting: nvfuser path is faster for heads but worse when tail needs kv-cache shuffling? Could be memory access pattern: nvfuser kernels assume contiguous KV pages; when we evict/rehydrate cache the memory stride changes and nvfuser launches a slower fallback. Need to check `kv_eviction_events` correlating with kernel flips.
perf-bot: perf telemetry query result: `avg_latency_up = +18%` for `kernel_flip` events in last 2h, `KV_EVICT_RATE` spiked from 0.02 -> 0.14. Link: https://perf.redwood/internal/q/abc123
Olivia P.: Can we try a change on runtime: add a small hysteresis window (e.g., require two consecutive sequence-length buckets before switching kernel) and see if that reduces oscillation? Also consider prioritizing memory-stable kernels when KV eviction rate > 0.1.
Ken L.: I'll prototype a hysteresis patch and run A/B tomorrow. Quick note: enabling `nvfuser_align_kv_pages=true` (local experiment) reduced fallback occurrences by ~60% and got tokens/s to ~330 on mixed runs.
Alex M.: Nice. Can you post the exact flag and the short repro command? I'll run on L40S too.
Ken L.: Command: `./run_infer --model gpt-small --precision fp8 --kernel-selector adaptive --nvfuser_align_kv_pages=1 --batcher=dynamic --microbatch=2 --trace=kernel_choice,kv_events`
Ken L.: Patch I'll try: add `selector_stability_counter` per-request and require >=2 confirmations before switching kernel. Keeps state in request context only.
Maria R.: Also add telemetry labels so we can measure: `selector_switch_reason` and `kv_eviction_at_switch` so perf dashboards can filter.
Olivia P.: Agreed. Action items: (1) Ken try hysteresis + align_kv_pages flag; (2) Alex run forced nvfuser/TE comparators on L40S; (3) Maria add telemetry labels and dashboard filters; (4) perf-bot will track `selector_switch_rate` and surface regressions.
Ken L.: Starting runs now, will drop short summary here once done. Thanks :thumbsup:
